what_the_writer_read:
Threat:
- ThreatFox, about the indicator only: 198.51.100.77:8443 (ip:port) is listed as win.nanocore, threat type botnet command and control.
- Background not evidence: NanoCore RAT: Windows remote-access trojan. The victim connects out to an operator-chosen host and port and speaks NanoCore's own protocol: length-prefixed, DES-encrypted frames over plain TCP. That channel carries no TLS handshake and never uses UDP.
- the flagged address 198.51.100.77 is in AS64510 Example VPS B.V. (NL).
Host:
- the address appears on 35 day(s) of campus history from 2026-10-21 to 2026-11-24, with traffic to or from a known remote address on 35.
- none of the products with a known purpose appears on its days of campus history.
- on 2026-11-22 it used 10 distinct services (the campus median was 13 and the 90th percentile 22) and moved 9.2 MB.
- names it used on the most of the 4 day(s) read, with the number of days: juniper-cloud.test (4), notify-hub.test (4), chalk-video.test (3), comet-games.test (3), drift-books.test (3), ember-code.test (3), ember-docs.test (3), hazel-health.test (3).
What happened:
- The host's contact with the flagged address: 3 distinct connections (address, port and name), 132 minute(s) on 2026-11-22..2026-11-24, first 2026-11-22 06:00 UTC, last 2026-11-24 23:30 UTC; 34.3 KB received, 55.2 KB sent.
- 198.51.100.77 carried at most 0 registered domain(s): not shown to be shared.
- From 2026-11-21 to 2026-11-24 (4 day(s)): after the first match the next destination new to this host was harbor-anchor-code.test, 13.6 h later; 3 new named destination(s) (this address used 10 distinct services on 2026-11-22, against a campus median of 13) and 1 network(s) with no name in all; uploads of 1 MB or more to new destinations: none.
- the distinct connections: 198.51.100.77 8443/TCP, no name, 36 minute(s), 9.4 KB received; 198.51.100.77 8443/TCP, no name, 48 minute(s), 12.6 KB received; 198.51.100.77 8443/TCP, no name, 48 minute(s), 12.4 KB received.
Outcome:
- Outcome: review. We kept this case for review because: a scheduled low-volume contact.
- 3 items; the first: scheduled low-volume contact with 198.51.100.77 on 2026-11-22: 36 minutes, mean gap 30.0 min, over 17.5 h.
- No ordinary reason found: 3 contact(s) with 198.51.100.77 (no TLS name, so no site can be named). In detail: no TLS name: the contact cannot be attributed to a site.
Next steps:
- Identify the device: the address lease (DHCP, network access control or VPN logs) for HOST from 2026-11-22 05:45 UTC to 2026-11-23 00:30 UTC, and on the later match day(s) 2026-11-23..2026-11-24. An address is not a device.
- Find which process makes the scheduled contact; a schedule this regular is a program, not a person.
- Identify the process behind contact 198.51.100.77 8443/TCP, no name at 2026-11-22 06:00 UTC.
- Check the host's endpoint record for a NanoCore client process and its persistence (a .NET executable started from the user profile) and for outbound TCP from it.

paragraphs.summary: ThreatFox lists 198.51.100.77 on port 8443 as win.nanocore, with threat type botnet command and control. A campus device made three connections to it between 22 Nov 2026 06:00 UTC and 24 Nov 2026 23:30 UTC. We kept the case for review because the contact recurs on a schedule and carries no TLS name, so no site can be named. The next step is to identify the device from its address lease for those dates.
paragraphs.threat: ThreatFox lists 198.51.100.77 port 8443 as win.nanocore, with threat type botnet command and control. Public sources describe NanoCore as a Windows remote-access trojan whose victims connect out to an operator-chosen host and port, speaking its own length-prefixed, DES-encrypted protocol over plain TCP with no TLS handshake and never UDP. The address sits in AS64510 Example VPS B.V. in the Netherlands.
paragraphs.host: Over 35 days from 21 Oct 2026 to 24 Nov 2026, the campus device had traffic to or from known remote addresses on every day we hold. On 22 Nov 2026 it used 10 distinct services and moved 9.2 MB. None of the products with a known purpose appears in its records, so we cannot say what kind of device it is.
paragraphs.contact: Between 22 Nov 2026 06:00 UTC and 24 Nov 2026 23:30 UTC the device made 3 connections to 198.51.100.77, all on port 8443 with no TLS name, lasting 132 minutes in total. It received 34.3 KB and sent 55.2 KB. We found no registered domain on this address, so we cannot show that it is shared.
paragraphs.why: We kept the case for review because the contact recurs on a fixed schedule: on 22 Nov 2026 it was a low-volume contact of 36 minutes with a mean gap of 30.0 minutes over 17.5 hours. Because no TLS name is present, we cannot attribute the contact to any site, and we found no ordinary reason for it.
paragraphs.after: From 21 Nov 2026 to 24 Nov 2026 the device reached 3 new named destinations; on 22 Nov 2026 alone it used 10 services, against a campus median of 13. The first new destination after the match was harbor-anchor-code.test, 13.6 hours later. It also reached one network with no name, and we found no uploads of 1 MB or more to new destinations.
paragraphs.conclusion: We can say the device contacted the listed address three times between 22 and 24 Nov 2026 and that these contacts recur on a schedule. We cannot say which program made them, whether the device runs NanoCore, or what the contacts carried, since no TLS name or other record shows it. The next steps are to identify the device from its address lease for 22 Nov 2026 05:45 UTC to 23 Nov 2026 00:30 UTC and on 23 to 24 Nov 2026; find which process makes the scheduled contact, starting at 22 Nov 2026 06:00 UTC; and check the device's endpoint record for a NanoCore client process, its persistence, and outbound TCP from it.
